The Company’s lead indication for 4D-150 is wet age-related macular degeneration, which is currently in Phase 3 development, and second indication is diabetic macular edema. The Company’s second product candidate is 4D-710, which is the first known genetic medicine to demonstrate successful delivery and expression of the CFTR transgene in the lungs of people with cystic fibrosis after aerosol delivery

GENERAL SUMMARY

Reporting to the Chief Medical Officer, the VP Clinical Development, Ophthalmology provides strategic and operational leadership for the global development of ophthalmic genetic medicines in Drug Development.

We seek an experienced physician to play a critical role at 4DMT as we spearhead the introduction of intravitreally delivered genetic medicines for the treatment of the most common causes of irreversible blindness. The VP, Clinical Development will be a primary point person for medical oversight of clinical studies, with responsibilities including medical monitoring, review and interpretation of clinical trial data, clinical trial design, protocol development, and drafting of key clinical documents such as protocols, CSRs, briefing packages, INDs, NDAs, BLAs, MAAs, and other regulatory documents. This role will be responsible for timely execution of deliverables in close collaboration with relevant internal and external partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide medical leadership for cross-functional internal workstreams including pharmacovigilance, biostatistics, clinical operations, regulatory affairs, etc.
  • Provide oversight and lead teams responsible for development plans, study protocols, amendments, ICFs, IBs, INDs, annual reports, CSRs, regulatory response documents, and other regulatory submissions or documents as appropriate.
  • Collaborate closely with Clinical Operations and be accountable for clinical trial conduct and timelines for associated key deliverables.
  • Keep up to date with compliance, SOPs and adhere to ICH, GCP, and relevant regulatory guidelines.
  • Provide medical leadership for internal audits and regulatory inspections.
  • Assist in preparation of materials for Advisory Board meetings, BOD meetings, etc
  • Represent 4DMT and lead interactions and collaborations with potential partners.
  • Represent the Ophthalmology Therapeutic Area with key external stakeholders, including patients and patient advocacy groups, external experts, investors, and the ophthalmic and biotech business communities
  • Travel domestically and internationally as required, approximately 20%. Other duties as assigned; nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Education:

  • MD Degree
  • Clinical training in Ophthalmology preferred
  • Retina fellowship training a plus
  • Board Certification (or equivalent) preferred

Experience:

  • Minimum of 8 years of biopharma industry experience in drug development.

  • Proven ability to plan and conduct clinical trials ensuring high-quality trial execution and results within established timelines; demonstrated track record working effectively in cross-functional teams and workstreams including pharmacovigilance, biostatistics, clinical operations, and regulatory affairs.

jobs.description:
What You'll Do

The Principal Compensation Partner, is a global, director-level individual contributor and a principal compensation subject matter expert for Avalara, supporting the Sales organization. This role sets the direction for global compensation strategy and designs the programs that bring it to life, with a particular focus on the compensation and incentive programs that drive GTM performance. The Principal Compensation Partner turns complex data into clear, compelling narratives that guide decisions, advising executives and senior leaders on the company’s most complex, sensitive, and high-impact compensation matters. This role ensures global compensation programs are competitive, equitable, compliant, and aligned with business strategy and talent objectives. This role operates with a high degree of independence, leads through influence rather than direct authority, and shapes compensation practices across the entire enterprise.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Use analysis and storytelling to drive decisions: turn complex compensation, market, and business data into clear, compelling narratives and executive-ready recommendations that shape decisions by senior leaders
  • Serve as the lead compensation partner and trusted advisor to the Sales organization, advising Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Sales Operations leaders on pay strategy, role structure, and talent attraction and retention for GTM roles.
  • Partner with GTM, Finance, and Sales Operations on the design, governance, and annual refresh of sales incentive programs, including pay mix, on-target earnings, quota and commission structures, and plan performance, ensuring they motivate the right behaviors and align with business goals.
  • Drive global compensation strategy and philosophy in partnership with People leadership, ensuring programs support business strategy, talent attraction and retention, and financial objectives, with a focus in the Sales organization.
  • Own and evolve Avalara’s sales job architecture framework and leveling governance, setting standards for job evaluation, EEO and FLSA classification, and internal equity, and making final determinations on the most complex and precedent-setting leveling decisions.
  • Partner with Finance on sales compensation budgeting, forecasting, and cost modeling, using advanced scenario analysis to evaluate the financial and talent impact of program decisions, including the cost and return of GTM incentive investments.
  • Conduct advanced compensation analysis to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and present findings with clear insight, a point of view, and a recommended course of action.
  • Lead and influence cross-functional, enterprise-wide initiatives by building alignment among senior stakeholders, managing risk, and driving measurable business outcomes.
  • Coach, mentor, and develop compensation team members and other senior individual contributors, setting standards for quality, analytical rigor, and storytelling, and sharing expertise across the People organization.
  • Optimizes AI tools used across compensation, and apply them to improve insight generation, compensation modeling, and executive reporting.

What You'll Need to be Successful

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field.

Experience

  • 15+ years of progressive compensation experience, including within a technology company.
  • Significant experience supporting a sales or go-to-market organization, including sales compensation or incentive plan design and administration.
  • Extensive experience designing and leading global compensation programs in a complex, multi-region environment.
  • Proven experience advising executives and senior leaders on complex, high-stakes compensation decisions.
  • Demonstrated track record of using data analysis and storytelling to influence senior-level decisions.
  • Experience leading large-scale, cross-functional initiatives with measurable business impact.
  • Experience coaching and developing compensation professionals.
  • Demonstrated experience using AI tools to enhance data analysis, reporting, modeling, or process efficiency.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Exceptional analytical and data storytelling skills, with the ability to distill complex data into clear narratives and visuals that drive decisions.
  • Expert knowledge of compensation principles, job architecture, market pricing methodologies, and incentive and equity program design.
  • Strong understanding of sales compensation principles, including pay mix, quota setting, commission and accelerator structures, and the link between incentives and sales performance.
  • Deep experience conducting market benchmarking using survey providers such as Radford, Mercer, and WTW, including strong command of survey methodology and data strategy.
  • Experience using Workday or similar Human Capital Management systems.
  • Advanced Excel skills, including modeling, scenario analysis, and executive-level reporting.
  • Strategic thinking and strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to anticipate business needs and frame recommendations in terms of business impact.
  • Knowledge of global compensation regulations and emerging legislative trends, including pay transparency and pay equity requirements.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment and discretion in highly ambiguous, sensitive, and high-impact situations.
  • Exceptional executive communication skills, with the ability to build credibility with senior leaders and influence without direct authority.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certified Compensation Professional (CCP) designation.
  • Experience supporting compensation programs in a public company environment, including exposure to executive compensation and Compensation Committee processes.
  • Experience in a high-growth or technology company, particularly a SaaS or subscription-based business.
  • Experience partnering with Sales Operations and Finance on sales incentive plan design and analytics.
  • Experience leading global compensation program design and structure, including through M&A integration or organizational change.
  • Experience conducting pay equity analysis and regulatory reporting.
  • Advanced degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, or a related field.

Avalara is an AI-first Company

AI is embedded in our workflows, decision-making, and products. Success here requires embracing AI as an essential capability.

  • You’ll bring experience using AI and AI-related technologies, ready to thrive here.

  • You’ll apply AI every day to business challenges - improving efficiency, contributing solutions, and driving results for your team, our company, and our customers.

  • You’ll grow with AI by staying curious about new trends and best practices, and by sharing what you learn so others can benefit too.

How We'll Take Care of You

Total Rewards

In addition to a great compensation package, paid time off, and paid parental leave, many Avalara employees are eligible for bonuses.

Health & Wellness Benefits vary by location but generally include private medical, life, and disability insurance.

Inclusive culture and diversity Avalara strongly supports diversity, equity, and inclusion, and is committed to integrating them into our business practices and our organizational culture. We also have a total of 8 employee-run resource groups, each with senior leadership and exec sponsorship.

What You Need To Know About Avalara

We’re defining the relationship between tax and tech.

We’ve already built an industry-leading cloud compliance platform, processing over 54 billion customer API calls and over 6.6 million tax returns a year. Our growth is real - we're a billion dollar business - and we’re not slowing down until we’ve achieved our mission - to be part of every transaction in the world.

We’re bright, innovative, and disruptive, like the orange we love to wear. It captures our quirky spirit and optimistic mindset. It shows off the culture we’ve designed, that empowers our people to win. We’ve been different from day one. Join us, and your career will be too.

An overview of this role

When a customer pushes a change, they need their CI/CD jobs to start quickly and run reliably, even when demand spikes. You'll help make that happen on GitLab.com by improving how Hosted Runners provision compute, isolate customer workloads, and recover from failures. Your decisions will shape how long customers wait for jobs to start and how efficiently GitLab uses cloud compute.

As a Senior Staff Site Reliability Engineer, you'll set technical direction across teams while continuing to write and operate production software in Go. You'll lead work across the runner control plane, worker provisioning, and job execution. Your primary focus will be GitLab.com, and you'll also provide technical leadership support for GitLab Dedicated Hosted Runners. You'll report to the engineering manager responsible for Hosted Runners.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Tuning autoscaling to reduce job wait times during demand spikes
  • Evaluating ways to isolate customer workloads
  • Improving how runner usage is measured for capacity planning and billing

What You'll Do

  • Lead architecture and delivery across teams. Plan migrations with representative workload tests, safe capacity handovers, and rollback paths.
  • Write, review, and ship Go code across GitLab Runner, autoscaling components, cloud integrations, and operational tooling.
  • Improve reliability from job pickup through cleanup. Join the Runners Platform on-call rotation, investigate failures across system layers, and verify fixes in production.
  • Work with Security and Runner engineers to evaluate workload isolation, balancing security and compatibility with performance and cost.
  • Build observability that connects the customer experience with fleet behavior and guides capacity decisions. Partner with Finance, Product, and the billing platform team on usage metering and cost attribution.
  • Reduce recurring operational work through automation, tooling, and runbooks that engineers can use independently.
  • Mentor experienced engineers through design, implementation, and operations. Clarify ownership across teams and help engineers validate AI-assisted changes before they reach production.

What You'll Bring

  • Recent hands-on experience building and operating production systems software such as controllers, agents, or schedulers. You've personally shipped code that handles challenges such as concurrency, retries, or resource cleanup.
  • Strong programming skills in Go or another systems language, with the ability to become productive in Go.
  • Deep Linux and networking knowledge. You can trace production failures across system layers and use measurements to validate fixes.
  • Experience operating Kubernetes in production, including diagnosing scheduling and resource issues and managing rollouts and recovery.
  • Experience building or operating autoscaled or dynamically scheduled compute, such as VM fleets, serverless platforms, or batch systems. You bring experience with public cloud and infrastructure automation or comparable fleet operations.
  • A working understanding of the CI job lifecycle and the implications of running customer-controlled code. You can bring that knowledge from outside a CI/CD team.
  • A record of leading technical initiatives across teams and personally contributing to implementation through production. You build agreement through clear writing and asynchronous collaboration, and mentor engineers to own what they build and operate.

About the team

Hosted Runners operates the compute behind customers' CI/CD jobs. You'll work with Runner Core to turn lessons from operating the fleet into improvements to the open-source GitLab Runner. You'll also work with Product and partner teams to agree on priorities and ownership for shared changes.

Overview

What We Believe

Millennium is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate or allow discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, citizenship, disability, veteran status or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law.

Responsibilities

Millennium Corporation is seeking a Cyber Security Engineer III to support cybersecurity, software assurance, and security engineering activities within a DoD/DoN environment. This position is 100% remote and will focus on integrating cybersecurity throughout the software development and delivery lifecycle, with an emphasis on application security, CI/CD pipeline security, container security, vulnerability management, and DoD cybersecurity compliance.

Candidates located in or near major U.S. Navy installations are preferred, with priority given to candidates in the New Orleans, Orlando, and Washington, DC metropolitan areas. Candidates located near other major Navy facilities may also be considered.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct code and container vulnerability assessments using approved DoD vulnerability scanning tools, DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs), Security Requirements Guides (SRGs), and other DoD/DoN software assurance tools.
  • Implement and assess operating system security configurations in accordance with applicable DISA STIGs and SRGs.
  • Perform cybersecurity assessments, security audits, and risk analyses to identify vulnerabilities and compliance gaps.
  • Apply security testing methodologies, including Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Review and implement cybersecurity policies and security controls within CI/CD pipelines to support secure software delivery and DoD/DoN requirements.
  • Serve as a GitLab security reviewer and approver for merge requests, reviewing security scan results and verifying that identified findings are remediated or appropriately documented through the approved risk-management process prior to release.
  • Review GitLab SAST, dependency, secret detection, and container scanning results; coordinate remediation activities with development teams and track findings through closure.
  • Review changes to GitLab security policies, pipeline controls, and protected branch settings to ensure required security checks and approvals remain properly enforced.
  • Provide cybersecurity oversight for containerized workloads using NeuVector, including review of vulnerability findings, admission control decisions, and runtime security alerts.
  • Collaborate with application and platform teams to investigate NeuVector findings, tune security policies, and document remediation actions or accepted risks.
  • Ensure security-related provisions within system acquisition and program documentation address identified cybersecurity requirements.
  • Provide cybersecurity guidance and assist with developing mitigation strategies for DoD information systems.
  • Prepare Risk Management Framework (RMF) artifacts and Memoranda of Agreement (MoAs) with system owners supporting interface and networking implementations.
  • Identify and evaluate Common Criteria and National Information Assurance Partnership (NIAP) certified technologies when applicable.
  • Evaluate cybersecurity products and technologies used by programs to validate compliance with applicable DoD/DoN requirements.
  • Support cybersecurity activities across the software lifecycle and collaborate with engineering, development, platform, and program teams to address security requirements and risks.

Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance.
  • Bachelor's degree with 8 years of relevant experience, or a high school diploma/equivalent with 13 years of relevant experience.
  • Experience working within the DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) and familiarity with DoDI 8510.01.
  • An Information Assurance Manager (IAM) Level II certification in accordance with DoD 8570.01-M, such as:-CISSP-GSLC-CISM
  • Experience with DoD cybersecurity requirements, including DISA STIGs and SRGs.
  • Experience with software security testing methodologies, including SAST and DAST.
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity within CI/CD or DevSecOps environments.
  • Experience with GitLab security tools and processes, including reviewing security scan results and supporting vulnerability remediation.
  • Candidates should be located in or near a major U.S. Navy installation. Preferred locations include New Orleans, LA; Orlando, FL; and the Washington, DC metropolitan area. Candidates near other major Navy facilities may also be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proficiency with GitLab, NeuVector, and Sonatype.
  • Experience with container security and vulnerability management.
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity within a DoD or Department of the Navy (DoN) environment.
  • Experience with the Navy's Rapid Assess and Incorporate Software Engineering (RAISE) methodology.
  • Experience with the RAISE Platform of Choice (RPOC).
  • Experience evaluating Common Criteria and NIAP-certified technologies.
  • Experience developing or supporting RMF artifacts, security documentation, and cybersecurity mitigation strategies.

Business Development

Assist with Business Development activities as required to support Millennium's strategic business objectives, which may include but not limited to participation in technical interviews, creation of technical documentation, general proposal writing support and proposal color reviews.

Physical Requirements

  • Must be comfortable with prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Must be able to lift up to 10-15 pounds at a time.

COMPENSATION:

$125,000- $135,000

The salary range provided for this position is intended as a general guideline and does not guarantee a specific salary or compensation amount. Final compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including, relevant education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities

jobs.description:
About Conduit

Conduit is an AI agent platform built for hospitality. Hotels, vacation rentals, and resorts use our agents for guest communication and internal operations, and those agents run millions of workflows a day.

Hospitality is 10% of global GDP, and guests judge it by how fast their requests get resolved. Resolving one usually means working across several tools and several people. Our agents do that coordination.

Role: Agent Strategy Manager

Some of our customers are property managers with no tech team. They hand us their guest support and operations, and we run them. Our agents do the work, and a remote team of virtual assistants picks up what the agents can't handle yet.

You own those customers after launch. You are the person they talk to every week, and you make sure they get more out of Conduit every month. You work as a pair with an Agent Deployment Strategist, who builds and tunes the agents. You own the relationship, the results the customer sees, and what we take on for them next.

Why this role is different

  • This is not a classic customer success role. You work in the product yourself: you read real guest conversations, find where the agent went wrong, and make the small fixes on our platform without waiting on anyone.

  • You own numbers, not just relationships: automation rate, guest outcomes, and how much more each customer runs on Conduit.

  • You help decide what we build next. Once we run a customer's guest support, we can take on dynamic pricing, getting their properties found in AI search answers, and accounting. You see which of these each customer needs first.

What the work looks like

  • Weekly check-ins with each customer on what the agents handled, what changed, and what comes next.

  • Turning customer feedback into agent changes, making the small ones yourself and scoping the bigger ones with your Agent Deployment Strategist.

  • Working with our Customer Ops team when something goes wrong, and making sure it doesn't happen twice.

  • Spotting where a customer can do more with us, and bringing in our sales team for the commercial side.

  • Writing down what works so every customer gets the same playbook.

Who you are

  • 3+ years in customer success, account management, technical account management, or implementation at a software or AI company. No hospitality background needed.

  • You have gone hands-on in the product you supported, not only managed the relationship.

  • You measure. You can tell us how you knew a customer was getting value, and what you did when they weren't.

  • You like operators and the people doing the work, and they trust you.

  • This role can be remote in the US, or in our San Francisco office. Candidates must be authorized to work in the US; we do not sponsor visas.

Compensation and Benefits

  • $100-180K base

  • 0.05%-0.15% equity

  • Performance bonus

  • Comprehensive health insurance and 401k match

  • Dinner covered every day

Interview Process

  • Intro call with the founders

  • Customer case with the founders: a customer is unhappy with what the agent did last week, and you work out what happened and what to tell them

  • Final round (onsite in San Francisco or virtual)

  • Culture fit conversation with the founders

  • References

jobs.excerpt: About Turing Turing’s mission is to accelerate superintelligence to drive real economic progress.
jobs.description:
About Turing

Turing’s mission is to accelerate superintelligence to drive real economic progress. Headquartered in San Francisco, Turing works with frontier AI labs to generate high-quality datasets, reinforcement learning environments, and frontier research benchmarks that improve model capabilities in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and advanced STEM reasoning. In software engineering, Turing is the largest and longest-running data provider in the category. Turing also works with Fortune 500 enterprises across financial services, life sciences, healthcare, retail, automotive, and CPG to build and deploy end-to-end agentic AI systems inside mission-critical workflows. By operating on both sides, Turing closes the loop between frontier research and enterprise deployment, turning real-world deployment signals into better data, evaluations, and more capable models. Learn more at .

The Role

Turing builds large-scale datasets and reinforcement learning (RL) environments that power post-training for the world's leading AI labs and enterprises.

The STEM Horizontal team produces the high-signal coding and STEM data frontier labs train on. We're looking for a Research Engineering Manager to lead the research engineering behind its next layer: synthetic data that measurably improves models, and new benchmarks that measure what today's evals miss.

You'll lead a team of research engineers, work side by side with research scientists, and stay close enough to the code to review an eval harness line by line or prototype a generator yourself when the team needs it. You'll also build the team: hiring research engineers is a core part of this role, not a side task. Ideally you've been on the other side, at a frontier lab, and know what makes a lab trust a dataset or a benchmark result.

  • Synthetic data that earns its place. Generation, verification, and filtering pipelines where every sample is checked, and where we can show which properties of the data drive downstream gains, not just how much of it we made.
  • Benchmarks that stay meaningful. New evaluations for capabilities current benchmarks miss, built with calibrated difficulty, contamination controls, and statistics strong enough that a lab can make a decision on the result.

Quality failures here are quiet. A subtle bug in a verifier doesn't crash anything; it ships thousands of wrong labels into someone's training run and costs weeks. If you want to build the team and the systems that catch that early, this is the seat.

What You'll Do

1. Build and Lead the Team

  • Build the team: define the profiles you need, run hiring, and grow research engineers selected for research taste as much as engineering rigor.
  • Run the team's operating rhythm: project selection, planning, experiment reviews, design docs, and clear ownership.
  • Coach engineers on experimental design, code quality, and presenting results; give direct, regular feedback and run fair performance cycles.
  • Define the standards the team works to: eval methodology, data quality bars, and reproducibility — every dataset and result can be regenerated from a commit, a config, and a seed.

2. Partner with Research Scientists

  • Turn hypotheses into experiment plans together: what we're testing, the baseline, the ablations, and the result that would change our minds.
  • Set the agenda with research scientists. You're expected to bring your own hypotheses, not only implement theirs.
  • Take research prototypes to production scale without losing the scientific intent.

3. Build Synthetic Data Systems at Scale

  • Own synthetic data pipelines that generate, verify, filter, deduplicate, and version data, combining programmatic generators, LLM-based generation, automated verifiers, and targeted expert review.
  • Judge data by its effect on models: ablations and fine-tuning or RL experiments that show which attributes (difficulty, diversity, correctness, coverage) drive gains.
  • Build quality systems that hold up at volume: gold sets, LLM-judge calibration against expert labels, sampling audits, and agreement metrics.

4. Create New Benchmarks and Evaluations

  • Find where frontier models fail and where existing benchmarks have saturated, and design evaluations that measure what's missing.
  • Own benchmark methodology end to end: task taxonomy, difficulty calibration, graders and verifiers, contamination controls, held-out splits, and confidence intervals.
  • Ship eval harnesses, including agentic and sandboxed-execution evals, that are deterministic, reproducible, and trusted by internal teams and partner labs.
  • Make the call on whether a result holds up: partner labs and internal teams act on your sign-off.
  • Publish benchmarks, datasets, and findings with our research scientists at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR.

5. Stay Hands-On and Work with Frontier Labs

  • Write code every week on the hardest, highest-leverage parts: core verifier logic, eval statistics, the pipeline component everything else depends on. Expect a third or more of your time on direct technical work.
  • Be the person the team brings its hardest debugging and methodology questions to: why a judge disagrees with experts, why an eval number moved, whether a gain is real or noise.
  • Act as a technical counterpart to researchers at frontier AI labs: scope requests, set acceptance criteria, and explain results and trade-offs plainly.
  • Partner with Strategic Project Leads, delivery, and engineering teams so research advances land in client work and in the platforms the team builds.

Sample Projects

  • Identify a capability gap, design and ship a benchmark for it, and see it adopted by partner labs.
  • Stand up a synthetic data pipeline for long-horizon coding tasks with execution-based verifiers, and run the ablations that show which task properties drive RL gains.
  • Calibrate an LLM-judge grading system against expert labels, map where it fails, and decide where humans stay in the loop.
  • Design the experiment that tells a partner lab whether a two-point gain on their eval is real.
  • Decide which of three competing synthetic data approaches the team should bet on, and design the experiments that settle it.

Tech Stack

  • Research: Python · PyTorch or JAX · SFT · DPO · PPO / GRPO · RL with verifiable rewards
  • Evals & data: LLM-as-judge · programmatic verifiers · sandboxed execution · gold sets · contamination checks
  • Platform: Python services (Django / FastAPI) · PostgreSQL · Docker · Terraform · AWS or GCP

What We're Looking For

  • Experience: 8+ years of hands-on ML or research engineering, at least 5 in industry, including 3+ years directly managing research engineers, ML engineers, or researchers (hiring and performance management included).
  • Synthetic data at scale: you've owned synthetic or curated data pipelines in production whose output drove training decisions, and can show how you measured their quality and downstream impact.
  • Evaluation rigor: you've designed and shipped LLM evals or benchmarks that others used to make model decisions, and understand contamination, saturation, judge bias, inter-annotator agreement, variance, and confidence intervals.
  • Experimental judgment: you plan ablations up front, choose baselines honestly, and can tell a real effect from noise.
  • Technical depth: strong Python; production experience with PyTorch or JAX; working knowledge of the post-training stack (SFT, DPO, PPO/GRPO, RL with verifiable rewards).
  • Technical direction: a track record of setting direction for a team, not only executing a roadmap handed to you.
  • Scale: distributed data processing and large evaluation or training jobs (e.g., Ray, Spark, Kubernetes) on AWS or GCP.
  • Communication: clear written communication for scientists and non-specialists alike; comfortable presenting results to researchers at partner labs.
  • AI-forward: daily use of LLM coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) as part of how you ship, with the judgment to review their output critically. This is a must-have.
  • Education: PhD or Master's degree in AI, machine learning, computer science, statistics, or a closely related field; PhD preferred. Exceptional equivalent research experience will also be considered. We weigh industry outcomes most heavily.

Strongly Preferred

  • Frontier AI lab experience: post-training data, evals, or reward modeling at a frontier lab (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI) or a top industry research group.
  • Built or contributed to a public benchmark or dataset the community uses.

Nice to Have

  • First-author papers at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, or similar.
  • RL environment and verifier design for agentic tasks: coding agents, tool use, computer use, long-horizon workflows.
  • Data valuation or attribution: measuring what each slice of data contributes to a model.
  • Depth in a STEM domain such as math, physics, chemistry, or biology (not required).
  • Experience managing tech leads or managers, or running several concurrent programs.
  • Directing large expert networks through specs, rubrics, and fast feedback loops.

A note from our CTO, Ece Kamar

Some of the most important questions in AI can't be answered from inside a single lab: how to evaluate frontier models, how data and RL truly drive capability, and what happens when AI meets the real world. At Turing, we work directly with frontier labs, the academic community, and enterprises deploying AI at scale. That creates a feedback loop where deployment shapes our research and our research shapes the field, and we publish our findings, datasets, and benchmarks openly. Join our talented team at Turing to push the frontier of AI with rigorous science that matters.

Why Turing

  • Work directly with leading AI labs and enterprises at the frontier of post-training, evaluation, and synthetic data.
  • Build the datasets and benchmarks that improve and measure the capabilities of advanced AI systems.
  • Shape how frontier labs measure progress on coding and STEM reasoning.
  • Operate with high autonomy, rapid iteration, and meaningful commercial impact.
  • Collaborate with exceptional colleagues from organizations including Google, Meta, Amazon, and other leading technology companies.
  • Contribute to research that may be shared through technical publications and leading conferences such as ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS.

Don't meet every single requirement?

BlackSky is trusted by the most demanding allied military and intelligence organizations and commercial companies to deliver foresight into critical matters that affect national security and the economy. BlackSky's data enables governments and businesses to see, understand and anticipate change as it happens, giving them the ultimate strategic advantage so they can act quickly. Our global team works with cutting-edge technology to make a difference around the world and prides itself on being people-first, customer-focused and fun.

BlackSky is looking for a strong, self-starting and eager engineer to join our Mission Planning Engineering team. This integrated product team is working to develop and maintain optimized autonomous operations for the BlackSky constellation. The Mission Planning Team works closely with the Mission Management SW Development team: Mission Planners own requirements documentation, initial scope and design documentation, and will lead SW feature development efforts by writing prototype code and/or written system level requirements which are executable by the SW development team. Strong candidates will have deep mission planning algorithm design experience, specifically for satellite or aerial imaging applications. Prior experience with different types of image planning logic, such as point targets, strip mapping, or pushbroom scanning or equivalent experience with time assignment problems is essential. The candidate should have solid experience in developing both prototype code and software system requirements.

In this role, you will develop and track system level requirements, schedules, and technical implementation for a wide variety of mission planning products and see them through to operation on orbit. Opportunities will exist for prototype code development in Python or Go, as well as internal tooling development for measuring KPIs, troubleshooting performance problems, and identifying and correcting inefficiencies in planning algorithms. While the primary responsibility of this hire will be to define system level and software requirements and prototype code, a strong background in production level software or embedded systems experience in spacecraft or autonomous vehicles will be valuable.

We have offices in Herndon, VA and Seattle, WA but are open to remote candidates.

Responsibilities:

  • Contribute to mission planning integrated product team, interfacing with mission planning, ground software, and operations and product engineers to plan and execute autonomous constellation operations software features.
  • Model, implement, and test concepts of operation for autonomous planning of various constellation activities including imaging, system calibration, propulsion, or other critical activities. This may involve leveraging heritage or building novel algorithms, as well developing new problem formulations to optimize image capture planning while respecting various other constraints and activities.
  • Model satellite subsystems (communications, power, attitude) using methods that are compatible with existing and future ground and control software algorithms as needed to support Mission Planning functions.
  • Support ongoing constellation operations and customer fulfillment efforts as a mission planning subject matter expert.
  • Translate product concepts to engineering requirements and facilitate review and discussion among engineering, product and software stakeholders.
  • Occasional 24/7 support expected during Launch and Early Operations or Anomaly Response in support of debugging and fixing mission planning algorithms.
  • Other relevant duties assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree or higher in one of the following fields: aerospace or mechanical engineering, systems engineering, computer science or equivalent.
  • At least six (6) years of relevant professional experience.
  • Experience with automation of complex systems (satellite, vehicle fleets, drones, shipping/delivery logistics etc.).
  • Experience with planning or optimization algorithms and fluency with inputs/outputs/constraints to such systems.
  • Experience writing technical requirements and driving to implementation.
  • Experience with project management or software product development.
  • Working knowledge of Go or Python.
  • Knowledge of software design, maintenance, and implementation including data structures, data retrieval and storage, algorithm efficiency, and maintainable scalable code.
  • Demonstrated initiative to identify and solve problems or inefficiencies in your current field of expertise.
  • Possess strong team and inter-team cooperation and organization skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a strong understanding of audience.
  • Ability to sustain a workload consisting of several concurrent, independent activities.
  • This program this role supports requires US citizenship.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Expertise in satellite or aerial imagery mission planning algorithms, specifically prior experience with point target, strip mapping, pushbroom, whiskbroom, wide area capture or stereo capture planning.
  • Fluent in satellite first principals such as orbital mechanics, attitude dynamics, and satellite systems.
  • Demonstrated experience with modelling/simulation projects.
  • Strong familiarity with orbital mechanics, attitude dynamics, and satellite systems.
  • Experience with planning algorithms and fluency with inputs/outputs/constraints to such systems.
  • Expertise with integer or linear program solvers.
  • Experience with embedded systems pertaining to satellites or other autonomous vehicles.
  • Experience with AI coding agents

Life at BlackSky for full-time benefits eligible employees includes:

  • Medical, dental, vision, disability, group term life and AD&D, voluntary life and AD&D insurance
    • BlackSky pays 100% of employee-only premiums for medical, dental and vision and contributes $100/month for out-of-pocket expenses!

BlackSky is a multi-state employer and this pay scale may not reflect salary ranges in other states or locations outside of Seattle, WA.

jobs.description:
Overview

The Workforce Management (WFM) Analyst is responsible for forecasting workload, planning staffing requirements, scheduling resources, and monitoring performance to ensure operational goals are achieved. The role partners closely with Operations, Training, Recruiting, and Business Leaders to optimize workforce utilization, service levels, customer experience, and operational efficiency.

Responsibilities

Forecasting & Capacity Planning

  • Develop short-term, mid-term, and long-term workload forecasts.

  • Perform staffing requirement calculations based on forecasts, Average Handle Time (AHT), service level targets, shrinkage assumptions, and occupancy goals.

  • Create capacity plans and hiring recommendations.

  • Conduct scenario modeling and what-if analyses.

Scheduling & Resource Planning

  • Design and optimize schedules.

  • Manage intraday staffing adjustments.

  • Monitor schedule adherence.

Real-Time Management

  • Monitor operational performance against key metrics.

  • Analyze trends and recommend corrective actions.

  • Partner with Operations to address staffing gaps and risks.

Reporting & Analytics

  • Develop dashboards and reports.

  • Analyze forecast accuracy, service level, Average Speed of Answer (ASA), Average First Response Time (AFRT), occupancy, shrinkage, adherence, and productivity metrics.

Stakeholder Management

  • Partner with leaders and present workforce insights.

  • Influence decisions through data-driven recommendations.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify process improvements and automation opportunities.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field.

  • 3+ years of WFM experience in a Contact Center / BPO environment.

  • Strong hands-on experience in Forecasting, Capacity Planning, Scheduling, and Real-Time Management.

  • Advanced Excel skills.

  • Experience with WFM platforms such as Verint, NICE IEX, Aspect, Genesys, Calabrio, or Alvaria.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting large-scale customer service, telecommunications, or technical support programs.

Key Competencies

  • Analytical Thinking: Strong forecasting and statistical analysis capabilities.

jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Staff Engineer, you'll be the technical anchor for GitLab's Nonlinear Productivity team in the US: the person who decides what "proven" means before something ships, and who helps shape what the team builds next, not just how to build it. It's a from-scratch, generalist team with no dedicated product manager — that ownership starts on day one.

Some examples of the problems this team takes on:

  • Cutting the time it takes to complete a good code review — one that still keeps a human in the loop — by half, using agentic solutions.
  • Turning a manual, error-prone release step into an agentic workflow that catches its own mistakes before a human ever has to.

What you'll do

  • Set the technical direction for the team's agentic systems, from how agents are orchestrated to where a step should stay human-owned, and defend those calls once they're tested against real code.
  • Discover and prioritize sources of friction across GitLab's SDLC, driving the fix — agentic, process-based, or both — from a rough hypothesis through to a shipped, measured result.
  • Work across any part of GitLab's codebase as the problem requires, since this team operates like a small, generalist group rather than one scoped to a single service.
  • Apply distributed systems judgment to catch cases where generated code looks correct but breaks under concurrency, at scale, or across deployment topologies (including self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant environments), and coach others to do the same.
  • Mentor senior and mid-level engineers on agent engineering practices and distributed systems judgment, through design reviews and pairing that raise the team's collective bar rather than just your own output.
  • Collaborate with the India-based group a few times a week to align on the roadmap, and represent the team's technical progress to stakeholders in the Chief Technology Officer's organization.
  • Serve as a bar raiser for the team's hiring, owning the Technical Leadership round for other Staff-level candidates as the team scales.
  • Own a greenfield technical foundation from day one, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.

What you'll bring

  • Experience building reliable agentic or large language model (LLM)-based systems, including multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery.
  • Ability to work autonomously in unfamiliar codebases and drive solutions from discovery through completion.
  • Strong distributed systems and computer science fundamentals, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.
  • Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, with the ability to read and modify code in the others.
  • A track record of delivering results from unclear or incomplete requirements — able to take a complex, loosely specified problem and decompose it into a concrete proposal of small, shippable steps.
  • Experience designing evaluation frameworks for systems where "looks plausible" and "is actually correct" are different questions, and a track record of raising the quality bar for a team's output, not just your own.
  • A history of unblocking and enabling teammates — through design reviews, technical writing, or mentoring — and of engaging regularly with other teams to find where collaboration actually pays off.

About the team

Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. Solutions that prove out internally are the team's path to a monetized, customer-facing GitLab offering.

It's a good fit for engineers who want technical ownership of something with no existing playbook, and a hand in defining a brand-new part of GitLab from its first commit.

jobs.title: Demand Generation Manager - 4 Day Week + Remote
jobs.excerpt: We have a full marketing production team.  Content, design, web, video, product marketing.
jobs.description:
We have a full marketing production team. Content, design, web, video, product marketing. We have a sales team sitting ready to take meetings. What we don't have is anyone whose entire job is filling the funnel.

So the pipeline gets built the hard way, one cold call at a time, while the inbound machine that should be feeding it doesn't exist yet.

We want one person to build it, own it, and be measured on what comes out of the end: qualified demos landing in the sales team's calendar.

This isn't a run-some-ads role. You'll own the whole journey, from people who've never heard of us, through people who know the name, all the way to a booked meeting. Paid, events, webinars, trade media, conversion, the handoff to sales, the budget and every number in between.

If you've built a demand gen engine before and want to do it again somewhere it will actually make the difference, keep reading.

Read on!

(this will be a long write up but we like to give you all the details before you spend your time applying)

We are Shape.Construction!

We are digitising the largest and most fundamental industry in the world, the industry that literally builds the foundations of the civilisation we all depend on to spare us from a brutal hunter-gatherer life: CONSTRUCTION

It is one of the least digitised industries in the world but also the largest – 1 in 9 people globally work in the construction industry and it constitutes 11% of global GDP.

Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Watch our short film about it).

We got our start as a high-end construction project management consultancy. As a consultancy, we are focused on genuinely upgrading the way construction projects are delivered. We then take the deep understanding of the projects we work on to develop construction management software products that anyone can use to deliver their projects better.

We are building a full suite of products one module at a time – kind of like office 365 but for construction management - Check out Shape, our construction management tech

The core of all this is our true secret sauce; people. We only recruit the very best both in capability and personality. We are deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that is optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People that join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined.

This approach has allowed us to grow from just 2 people in 2017 to over 120 today (including consultancy) and we are still very much at the beginning! Joining us isn't just some "job", it is a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life.

4 core values for a good life

We believe a life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships with others and challenging yourself to create a positive impact. So our values reflect the 4 levels of relationships that each of us has:

  • Grow yourself – Your relationship with yourself
  • Care about people – Your relationship with others around you
  • Execute to greatness – Your relationship with your team
  • Build civilisation – Your relationship with humanity and the world

This goes much deeper but for the sake of brevity, we will keep the summary version!

We enshrined our values in our vision

We exist so that everyone in our team can thrive in a high-impact community that:

  • Connects us with meaningful relationships
  • Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans
  • Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures

We believe that, by first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world.

And enable the achievement of our vision through our dual missions:

  1. To fully digitise the construction of human civilisation
  2. To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society

The Role

Purpose of the role

Shape has a full marketing production team (content, design, web, video, product marketing) and a sales team ready to take meetings. What we don't have is someone whose entire job is filling the funnel. You'll own one number, qualified demos booked for the sales team, and everything that feeds it.

This isn't a run-some-ads role. You'll build and own the complete journey from cold audiences who've never heard of us, through "Shape Aware" (people who've engaged with the brand: visited the website, engaged with content or ads), all the way to a booked demo. You own the funnel, the numbers at every stage of it, and how those leads land with the sales team.

Team

You'll sit in Shape's marketing team and your leader will be the Head of Marketing. You'll work daily with the SDR and sales teams, who receive everything you generate.

The team already has content, design, web, video and product marketing covered, so you won't be writing the copy or building the pages yourself. You'll brief and direct that output toward campaigns. You'll also work alongside our GTM Engineer, who owns the data and signals layer you'll use to target the right accounts at the right time.

What's missing is someone pointing all of that at a number. That's you.

Your top six objectives

  1. Own inbound lead generation end to end, with qualified demos booked for the sales team as your core KPI.

  1. Build a full funnel we can see into at every stage, from cold audiences through Shape Aware to booked demo.

  1. Run paid as your fastest route to volume: advertising is your primary engine.

  1. Build events, webinars, trade media and syndication into a second engine, so we're not dependent on ad spend alone.

  1. Own conversion and the handoff, so no lead ever goes stale in a form somewhere.

  1. Own the budget: recommend what spend is needed to hit the number, then justify, track and report on it.

Your top six responsibilities

Your remit splits into two activity streams, Paid and Events, and you decide the right mix between them based on what's actually producing demos. Beyond those two, you own the full channel mix. If you see an opportunity in SEO, partnerships, referral, PR or review sites that gets us to the number faster, that's yours to pursue too.

  1. Advertising.LinkedIn, Google, Meta, Reddit, Insta and any other channel worth running, both cold acquisition and retargeting to warm Shape Aware audiences.

  1. Paid media and syndication. Trade publications and industry media placements that put us in front of the right audience.

  1. Events coordination.Choosing and running the industry events and conferences worth being at, from planning through to the follow-up that turns attendees into demos.

  1. Webinars, in two formats.One-to-many webinars on product demos and industry topics for top and mid-funnel, building the Shape Aware audience and warming people up. And one-to-few "lunch and learn" style sessions for a small group of target accounts at the bottom of the funnel, run in support of sales to help move specific deals forward.

  1. Funnel, conversion and handoff. Build and report on funnel-stage metrics, not just the demo number: how many people are Shape Aware, how they move between stages, where they drop off and what it costs to move them. Own conversion, so landing pages, forms and follow-up journeys, testing and iterating relentlessly. Own the handoff, so when a demo is booked you define how the sales team is notified, what context they get and how fast it happens.

  1. Budget, briefing and lead quality. Recommend what spend is needed across channels to hit the number and justify it, then track and manage it, reporting on cost per demo, cost per stage and pipeline generated. Direct our content and design teams' output toward campaigns with briefs for ad copy, landing pages, lead magnets and nurture assets. Work with the SDR team on lead quality, so demos are ones sales actually wants. Use our data and signals layer, built by our GTM Engineer, to target the right accounts at the right time.

Your Capabilities

You are a demand gen operator who has done this before and can do it again from a standing start. You think in funnels and unit economics rather than campaigns and impressions, and you'd rather bring a playbook you've already proven than experiment your way into one on our budget.

Must-Have (The fundamentals)

  • Mastery:A track record building full-funnel B2B demand generation, not just managing ad spend. You will show how you took cold audiences through to booked meetings and the numbers at each stage. Hands-on paid media experience (LinkedIn Ads and Google Ads as a minimum) and a strong grasp of conversion optimisation across landing pages, forms and follow-up journeys. Ideally some experience with events, webinars or trade media as lead sources. HubSpot experience a strong plus.
  • Communication: Proficient communicator in written and verbal English. Able to brief and direct creative teams without doing the design or copy yourself, and to report honestly upward on what's working and what isn't.
  • Leadership:Strong critical thinking. You work out why something isn't converting and fix the right problem, rather than turning dials and hoping. You're comfortable owning a number and being measured on it, and you lead yourself proactively.
  • Impact:AI-native in how you work. You use AI (we run on Claude, including Claude Cowork) to handle the admin, reporting and grunt work so your time goes on strategy and optimisation. If you're still doing manually what an AI can do, this isn't the role for you.

Nice to Have (If you don't have it now you will after joining)

  • Mastery:Marketing automation and nurture design in HubSpot, account-based marketing into named accounts, SEO and organic as a lead source, and construction or built-environment industry knowledge (a bonus, not a requirement).
  • Communication:The confidence to influence a sales team on lead quality and definitions, rather than just handing leads over and hoping.
  • Leadership:Experience being the first demand gen hire somewhere, building the function from nothing rather than inheriting one.
  • Impact:A repeatable playbook you've run more than once, at more than one company, with the numbers to show it worked both times.

Shape isn't the place for you if any of the following is true:

  • You want an easy role without much challenge
  • You like to be the smartest person in the room
  • You don't like continuously receiving honest candid feedback
  • You prefer to do your own thing rather than work with a team
  • You'd rather report on activity than be measured on an outcome

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you tell me more about what the role is like?
We are in scale up mode so it will be a full-on role with more things to do than time available.
This is why it will be important to prioritise ruthlessly. We don't like to mess about so you will need to be a very high performer who only wants to work with others of your ilk.
This role is unusually clear about what success means, because it comes down to one number. That's a good thing if you like owning an outcome and having the autonomy to decide how you hit it. We are growing rapidly so that means your role will grow rapidly too. You will need to keep up and constantly be looking 1-2 years ahead.
What does success look like?
Within 3 months: a measurable funnel we can see into at every stage. How many people are Shape Aware, what it costs to create them, how they convert, and a predictable flow of demos landing with sales, with the team notified instantly and properly every time one books.
As for a tangible target, you are generating 30 qualified demos a month via inbound activity, with the months leading up showing a clearly defined path to that number and significant, visible improvement week on week.
Realistically we expect paid to be the fastest route there, but how you hit the number is your call. Beyond that, we want events and webinars contributing properly so the number keeps growing and we aren't dependent on ad spend alone.
What have you already got in place?
A full production team for content, design, web and video, so you have people to build what you brief. HubSpot as our CRM and marketing platform. A GTM Engineer building out our data and signals layer, so you'll have account and intent data to target with rather than guessing. What we haven't had is anyone owning the funnel itself, which is why the channels are underused and the reporting doesn't yet exist.
Where would I be working?
All our roles are 100% remote and home-based. However, if you would like to work in a co-work space to get out of the house we may be able to arrange that. If you are in one of our locations with offices, you can come as often as you like.

Benefits

The Standard Stuff

  • Health Insurance Scheme. Comprehensive private health coverage - for you and your family. Because your well-being is our priority
  • Bonus Scheme. As a permanent member of the team, you’ll share in our success. Our annual bonus is designed to reward both the now and the future - with a flexible mix of cash and high-growth equity that you choose. Bonuses are discretionary and based on performance
  • Professional body membership. One fee covered per year - so you can stay connected to your field and develop your craft

The Life-Changing Stuff

  • In-house coaching: Regular 1:1 coaching sessions, fully confidential, to help you navigate challenges, build self-awareness, and grow intentionally - professionally and as a human being
  • Flexibility: Getting things done is what really matters, not what time of day you do it. That means you don’t have to ask permission for things like picking up your kids or going to the doctor, just keep your team in the loop if you think they will be affected.
  • Grow your whole self: Our leaders are more like coaches and one of our main objectives is to give 5 years’ worth of learning and development for every 1 year with us. You have a coach, mentor, well-being therapist and a development-orientated environment: That’s literally what our vision is all about and the primary reason Laminar exists.
  • Be surrounded by the best: We only hire and retain the very best people. You might be used to being the smartest in the room but that won’t be the case in Laminar. You will be surrounded by people you can learn from. We are 100% meritocratic so fast progression is the norm. You will be supported to excel in whichever areas you are most interested in! With Laminar, development is unbounded
  • Long-term impact: We are focused on solving the biggest issues in construction project delivery in a way that can spread and outlast us

Important! Applying properly

We get thousands of applications so please write us a letter as part of your application explaining:

  • Why do you want to join us?
  • What do you think you bring to the team?
  • Tell us about a demand gen playbook you've run that worked, and the numbers it produced

We aren't a giant faceless corporation; we really care about the people who want to join our team so all letters will be read thoroughly.

After that, we will reach out to you to schedule a casual conversation to help you to know us a bit better and tell us a bit about yourself.

After that, we will schedule a couple of technical and personal assessments to understand what your level of capability is based on our own development matrix. This is to ensure that when you join you are starting at the right level of responsibility based on your capability not just based on experience.

jobs.title: Senior Financial Analyst
jobs.excerpt: ABOUT ALU ALU provides higher education for a higher purpose.
jobs.description:
ABOUT ALU

ALU provides higher education for a higher purpose. Our students declare missions, not majors.They develop the real-world skills to take on the world’s most pressing challenges. And they take ownership of their learning from day one through our peer and student-led approach – because ALU believes in the power and agency of young people to start shaping the future right now. Together with a world-class faculty and staff, our students are igniting a ripple of positive impact across Africa and the world.

We are dedicated to fostering an open yet secure environment, balancing the safety of students, staff, and visitors with respect for individual rights, and safeguarding responsibilities.

HOW WE WORK

The ALU Team works in starkly different ways to traditional academic bureaucracies. We approach education from first principles, empower individuals to design, test, and implement creative new ideas, and work closely together to craft transformative learning experiences. We are deeply passionate about our students and excited by the challenge of building something entirely new.

The African Leadership University is committed to ensuring the safety and Well-being of all students under our care. As part of this commitment , we have a comprehensive safeguarding policy in place , which outlines our Zero-tolerance approach to any violation of safeguarding.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Senior Financial Analyst brings business acumen and commercial judgment to the Financial Performance & Reporting team. This senior analyst owns the topline revenue intelligence function, tracking, interpreting, and communicating student revenue performance, collections trends, and financial outcomes to institutional leaders. Working under the Associate Director of Financial Performance & Reporting, you will transform reconciled data into performance narratives, manage the donor and grant reporting relationship, and serve as a thought partner to academic and operational stakeholders.

This is a role for a finance professional with strong business instincts, excellent communication skills, and the ability to comfortably sit at the intersection of numbers and strategy. You make the data mean something to the people who need to act on it.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

Topline Revenue Performance Management

  • Own the monthly revenue performance reporting cycle: student fee revenue, collections rates, discount trends, deferred income movements, and receivables ageing.
  • Develop and maintain revenue intelligence dashboards tailored to senior management and Board audiences — translating complex data into clear performance narratives.
  • Track and analyse student cohort revenue trends, segmented by programme, campus, scholarship status, and payment modality.
  • Identify revenue risks and opportunities (collection gaps, billing anomalies, discount leakage) and present actionable recommendations to the Associate Director and VPF.
  • Monitor and report on collections performance against targets; provide weekly/monthly collections summaries to the Finance Operations team and leadership.
  • Partner with the Registrar and Enrolment teams to align financial forecasts with academic and student data, ensuring one coherent revenue picture.

Management Reporting & Financial Performance Analysis

  • Lead the preparation of monthly management accounts commentary and quarterly Board financial packs — ensuring narrative clarity, actionable insights, and variance explanations.
  • Conduct variance analysis and trend identification across revenue and expenditure lines; develop and present narratives for senior management and Board reporting.
  • Reconcile statutory financial statements with management accounts to ensure consistency between compliance reporting and internal performance data.
  • Support the Associate Director in preparing forward-looking analysis: investment cases, cost optimisation opportunities, and resource allocation recommendations.
  • Produce ad-hoc financial analysis and scenario modelling to inform strategic decisions, new programme launches, and funding proposals.

Donor & Grant Reporting

  • Own donor financial reporting end-to-end: prepare accurate, timely donor reports, ensuring transparency on fund receipt, allocation, and utilisation.
  • Partner with the Fundraising and Programme teams to track fund collections, expenses, and budget vs actuals per grant — reconciling financial records with donor commitments.
  • Develop new programme budgets for grant applications in collaboration with the Fundraising team, aligned with ALU's strategy and chart of accounts.
  • Review draft financial reports from the Data Analyst, add narrative and context, and finalise for submission under the Associate Director's oversight.
  • Serve as the relationship interface between the Finance team and Fundraising/Programme teams on grant compliance matters.

Financial Planning & Forecasting

  • Co-lead the annual budgeting cycle with the Associate Director: facilitated departmental submissions, challenged assumptions, and consolidated institutional forecasts.
  • Maintain rolling revenue forecasts, integrating enrolment projections, collections assumptions, and pricing changes into forward-looking models.
  • Support sensitivity analysis and long-term sustainability modelling, contributing business judgment to technical models built by the Data Analyst.
  • Translate strategic priorities into financial targets and contribute to the institutional performance framework.

Business Partnering & Stakeholder Management

  • Act as a thought partner to academic and operational leaders on financial performance, surfacing risks and improvement opportunities in plain language.
  • Support in preparing Board and ExCo financial presentations, ensuring data accuracy, visual clarity, and strategic framing.
  • Partner with the Business Planning & Transformation teams to integrate financial KPIs into institutional performance dashboards and planning cycles.
  • Collaborate with the Finance Operations Director (FOD) to ensure smooth handoffs between operational transactions and management reporting.
  • Support external stakeholder reporting (Board, regulators, donors) with validated data and clear analysis.

Tools & systems

Tool

Expected Use

NetSuite (ERP)

Extract AR ledger, grant-coded transactions, deferred income data; run saved searches and exports

Google Sheets / Google Suite

Primary working environment for all trackers, reconciliations, dashboards, and reporting files

SQL

Working knowledge query writing for data extraction and reconciliation (advantage)

Salesforce

Extract billing, opportunity, and payment data; validate against NetSuite; support donor register

Google Suite (Slides / Docs)

Format dashboards and reports for leadership and donor audiences

Excel

Advanced financial modelling, scenario analysis, and sensitivity tables

Power BI (desirable)

Build or contribute to institutional financial dashboards as the function matures

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

Essential qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • 5–7 years of experience in financial management, FP&A, or management reporting — with demonstrated business partnering experience.
  • Strong financial reporting and analysis skills: variance analysis, management accounts, Board reporting.
  • Experience working with revenue-generating operations: student fees, subscriptions, project-based income, or equivalent.
  • An excellent written and verbal communication applicant needs to be able to translate financial complexity into clear narratives for non-finance audiences.
  • Experience managing donor or grant financial reporting, including budget vs actuals and utilisation tracking.
  • Strong grounding in financial accounting and reporting principles, with the ability to challenge and validate underlying numbers
  • Prior experience in audit (Big Four preferred) or a role with significant exposure to financial close and reporting processes
  • Demonstrated experience supporting or owning month-end close processes in a structured environment
  • High attention to detail with a focus on data integrity, controls, and completeness
  • Ability to operate across both analytical (FP&A) and control/reporting environments
  • Comfortable working with ERP systems (e.g., NetSuite) and large datasets, with an understanding of how transactions flow into reporting
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to enforce deadlines and challenge slippage constructively

OTHER COMPETENCIES

Desirable qualifications

  • Experience in education, non-profit, or international development financial environments.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce for revenue and pipeline tracking.
  • Exposure to institutional performance frameworks, KPI design, and balanced scorecard approaches.
  • Understanding of revenue recognition principles, deferred income, and student receivables accounting.
  • Power BI or data visualisation tool experience (consuming dashboards and shaping requirements).

Personal Attributes

  • Commercial and strategic thinker: connects financial data to institutional outcomes and business decisions.
  • Exceptional communicator: writes and speaks with clarity and precision for executive audiences.
  • Relationship builder: trusted by academic and operational leaders as a credible finance partner.
  • Ownership mindset: takes accountability for the quality and timeliness of reporting outputs.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and foundational work: able to build structure in a function that is still being established.
